overview: A Kungurian articulated holotype combining frog-like and salamander-like features and recovered as a stem batrachian in the original analysis.

ecology.diet: Small-prey feeding inferred from anatomy; direct diet unavailable
ecology.habitat: Clear Fork Group depositional context; detailed niche unresolved
ecology.locomotion: Terrestrial or semiaquatic performance not directly measured
ecology.guild: Inferred small predator; not directly observed

evidenceSummary: USNM 489135 is a uniquely informative individual, but its stem-batrachian placement is analysis-dependent and does not settle lissamphibian origins.

overview: An Early Triassic stem salientian known from one split-nodule holotype re-examined with micro-CT.

ecology.bodySize: Small holotype preserved in part and counterpart

evidenceSummary: MNHN.F.MAE.126 records a stem-salientian mosaic and hidden anatomy, while provenance, stage-scale dating and locomotor interpretation remain bounded.

overview: An Oxfordian salamandroid genus represented by one holotype and five referred articulated specimens, including material with larval structures.

ecology.habitat: Tiaojishan Formation depositional setting; niche unresolved
ecology.locomotion: Aquatic or semiaquatic inference remains specimen-dependent

evidenceSummary: PKUP V0601–V0606 support salamandroid placement and a neoteny interpretation, but the zircon age comes from overlying rock and both placement and development remain analysis-sensitive.

overview: A Norian stem gymnophionomorph represented by isolated three-dimensional bones from at least seventy-six individuals in one dated bonebed.

ecology.diet: Small-prey feeding inferred, not directly observed
ecology.habitat: Bonebed depositional context; burrowing and niche remain inferential
ecology.bodySize: Small-bodied individuals represented by isolated elements

evidenceSummary: The large disarticulated sample and U–Pb-bracketed locality support a caecilian total-group record and one dissorophoid-origin analysis without dating crown Gymnophiona or settling all lissamphibian-origin models.
